en: a. having a strong, sharp, often unpleasant taste; making you feel angry or unhappy because of a bad experience; (of weather) very cold; adv. extremely (cold); v. to make or become bitter
ex: The coffee tasted bitter without any sugar.
這杯咖啡不加糖喝起來很苦。

en: to design or create something that did not exist before; to make up a story or excuse that is not true
ex: Who invented the telephone?
電話是誰發明的？
ph: necessity is the mother of invention

en: a. relating to the activity of sex or the body parts involved in it; relating to the differences between men and women
ex: The company has a strict policy against sexual harassment.
公司對性騷擾有嚴格的政策。

en: adv. in or into a building; inside a house or building
ex: It started to rain, so we went indoors.
開始下雨了，所以我們進到室內。

en: to make a decision about something; to find out the facts about something; to control or influence what happens; to be the cause of something
ex: The judges will determine the winner tomorrow.
評審明天將決定優勝者。

en: n. a person whose job is to prepare a book, newspaper, film or other thing for publishing; a person who is in charge of a newspaper or a section of it; a computer program for changing text
ex: The editor corrected several errors in the article.
編輯修正了文章中的幾處錯誤。

en: a. frightening; (informal) easily frightened; causing fear
ex: The haunted house was really scary at night.
那棟鬼屋在夜裡真的很恐怖。

en: n. a small round nut that grows underground and is eaten roasted or made into butter or oil; (peanuts) a very small amount of money; a. very small
ex: He is allergic to peanuts, so he never eats them.
他對花生過敏，所以從不吃。

en: n. a place where unwanted waste is taken and left; a very untidy or unpleasant place; v. to drop or put down something in a careless way; to end a relationship with someone; to sell goods in large amounts at low prices
ex: The old refrigerator was thrown into the dump.
舊冰箱被丟進垃圾場。

en: a large tropical fruit with a rough brown skin, spiky leaves and sweet yellow flesh
ex: We had fresh pineapple for dessert.
我們飯後吃了新鮮的鳳梨當甜點。

en: n. an informal name that people use instead of someone's real name; v. to give someone an informal name
ex: His friends gave him the nickname Tiny because he was so tall.
他的朋友因為他很高大而叫他小不點。

en: a. relating to towns and cities; characteristic of a city rather than the countryside
ex: More and more people are moving to urban areas.
越來越多人搬到都市地區。

en: n. a place where people go to drink alcohol and sometimes eat a meal, especially in Britain
ex: We stopped at a pub for a drink after work.
下班後我們去酒館喝一杯。

en: a. funny and enjoyable; having or showing a sense of humor
ex: She wrote a humorous story about her first day at school.
她寫了一篇關於第一天上學的幽默故事。

en: n. the person who is elected to lead the government of a town or city
ex: The mayor made a speech at the opening of the new library.
市長在新圖書館的開幕典禮上致詞。

en: v. to break suddenly with a sharp noise; to speak sharply or angrily; to take a photograph; to make a sharp sound; n. a sudden sharp sound; a photograph; a short period of cold weather
ex: The branch snapped under the weight of the snow.
樹枝被雪的重量壓斷了。

en: n. the quality of being physically strong; the power of a person or group to do something; a good quality of someone or something; the degree of force or intensity; the number of people in a group
ex: He used all his strength to push the heavy door open.
他用盡全力把沉重的門推開。

en: n. a thick soft covering for a floor or stairs; a layer of something that covers a surface; v. to cover a floor with a carpet; to cover a surface completely
ex: They bought a new carpet for the living room.
他們為客廳買了一張新地毯。

en: a building with glass walls and roof used for growing plants that need protection from the cold
ex: Tomatoes grow well in a greenhouse.
番茄在溫室裡長得很好。

en: v. to be all around someone or something; to be near someone or something on all sides; to be with someone or something everywhere; n. an area or object that goes around something
ex: The house is surrounded by tall trees.
那棟房子被高大的樹木環繞著。

en: conj. if something does not happen or is not true; except when; prep. (formal) other than
ex: You won't pass the test unless you study hard.
除非你用功讀書，否則考試不會及格。

en: n. a four-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses; a railway passenger car; the way a person holds his or her body; the cost of carrying goods
ex: The bride arrived at the church in a horse-drawn carriage.
新娘乘著馬車抵達教堂。

en: n. a group of people who watch or listen to a performance, speech or broadcast; the people who read a book or magazine; a formal meeting with an important person
ex: The audience clapped loudly after the concert.
音樂會結束後觀眾熱烈鼓掌。

en: a. happening all the time or repeatedly; staying at the same level; always loyal; n. a number or amount that does not change
ex: The constant noise from the street kept me awake.
街上持續不斷的噪音讓我睡不著。

en: v. to make a liquid flow out of a container; (of liquid) to flow quickly; (of rain) to fall heavily; (of people) to come or go in large numbers; n. the act of pouring
ex: She poured a glass of milk for her son.
她為兒子倒了一杯牛奶。

en: a. well known to you; often seen, heard or experienced; having good knowledge of something; (of a person) friendly or informal; n. a person's close friend or companion
ex: Her face looks familiar, but I can't remember her name.
她的臉看起來很眼熟，但我想不起她的名字。

en: the yellow part in the middle of an egg
ex: Separate the yolk from the egg white before mixing.
先把蛋黃和蛋白分開再攪拌。

en: n. a country or area controlled by another, more powerful country; a group of people who settle in a new land; a group of animals or insects living together; a group of people with the same interests living together
ex: India was once a British colony.
印度曾是英國的殖民地。

en: n. a wide street, often with trees on each side; a way of reaching or achieving something; (US) a road in a town
ex: Fifth Avenue is one of the most famous avenues in New York.
第五大道是紐約最有名的大街之一。

en: adv. in a short time from now or after something has happened; in a few words; in a rude or impatient way
ex: The train will arrive shortly, so please wait on the platform.
火車即將抵達，請在月台上等候。

en: v. to make cloth by crossing threads over and under each other; to put things together to make something complete; to move along a winding path; n. a way of weaving cloth
ex: She learned to weave baskets from her grandmother.
她跟奶奶學會編籃子。

en: n. a structure like a wall made of wood or wire that surrounds a garden or field; a person who buys and sells stolen goods; the sport of fighting with thin swords; v. to surround an area with a fence; to fight with thin swords; to avoid giving direct answers
ex: A wooden fence surrounds the garden.
一道木籬笆圍繞著花園。

en: a. good enough for a particular purpose; making you feel pleased; acceptable
ex: The results of the experiment were satisfactory.
實驗結果令人滿意。

en: n. either of the two soft parts of your face below your eyes; (informal) a rude or too confident way of behaving; either of the two sides of your bottom
ex: She kissed her baby on the cheek.
她親了寶寶的臉頰。

en: n. all the actors in a play or film; the act of throwing something; a hard cover that supports a broken bone; an object made by pouring liquid metal into a mold; v. to throw something; to cause light or shadow to fall on something; to choose actors for a play or film; to shape metal by pouring it into a mold
ex: The cast of the film includes several famous actors.
這部電影的演員陣容包括幾位知名演員。

en: to pause before you do something, usually because you are nervous or not sure; to be unwilling to do something
ex: Don't hesitate to ask if you have any questions.
如果有任何問題，請儘管詢問。

en: v. to put your arms around someone and hold them tightly; to stay very close to something; n. an act of holding someone tightly in your arms
ex: She gave her mother a big hug at the airport.
她在機場給了媽媽一個大擁抱。

en: a person who studies or writes about history; an expert in history
ex: The historian wrote a book about the ancient Roman Empire.
這位歷史學家寫了一本關於古羅馬帝國的書。

en: a. fair and sensible; (of a price or amount) not too expensive or too large; able to think in a sensible way
ex: The restaurant serves delicious food at a reasonable price.
這家餐廳以合理的價格供應美味的食物。

en: a. not new; having had a previous owner; (be used to) familiar with something so that it no longer seems strange
ex: He bought a used car because it was much cheaper.
他買了二手車，因為便宜多了。
